$comment: HAND-TRANSCRIBED, and every row here is an EXPLICIT NON-PRICE. Not one atlascloud model ships a
`cost` in src/providers/atlascloud/models.ts, and this file is the recorded reason.
THE CONTRADICTION, in Atlas's own words. Each model page is a React application whose shipped
bundle carries THREE mutually exclusive price sentences from three templates (read at
https://www.atlascloud.ai/models/bytedance/seedance-2.5/reference-to-video on 2026-08-26,
verbatim from the page source):
1. "Your request will cost ${price} per run. For $10 you can run this model approximately
{times} times."
2. "For every second of 720p video you generated, you will be charged ${rate}/second. Your
request will cost ${tokenRate} per 1000 tokens. The number of tokens is given by (height of
output video x width of output video x (input duration + output duration) x 24) / 1024. If
video inputs are provided the rate drops to ${tokenRateWithVideo} per 1000 tokens. With video
inputs and 720p resolution the price is ${rateWithVideo} per second."
3. the same page's meta description: "Starting from $0.134/1M tokens" — for the model whose card
in the related-models strip reads "From $0.134 /SEC".
One number, 0.134, presented as a per-run price, a per-second rate and a per-million-token rate on
one page. That is not ambiguity a careful reader can resolve; it is three different products.
AND THE CATALOG CANNOT SETTLE IT. GET https://api.atlascloud.ai/api/v1/models returns a `price`
object per row, but only 2 of 337 media rows carry `price.actual.unit` (both "generation", both
MiniMax audio rows); the other 335 are a bare `base_price` STRING with no unit at all. And 152 of
473 rows carry a promotional `discount` between 40 and 90, so `price.actual` is not the list price
either — it is today's offer.
SO EVERY ROW IS `unpriced`, under the same rule that governs data/fal/pricing.json: a rate needs a
source, a date and the quote it was read from, or the row ships no rate. What is carried instead is
what Atlas actually published — `listed.actual`, `listed.origin` and `listed.discount`, transcribed
verbatim and explicitly UNIT-LESS. `src/providers/atlascloud/pricing.ts` re-states the same table
as ATLASCLOUD_LISTED_BASE_PRICE_USD beside ATLASCLOUD_PRICING_CAVEAT, and
`atlascloud.video` declares NO `estimate` at all — a function that always returns `undefined` is a
promise that a number is coming, and a missing one is the truth.
READ `listed.discount` CAREFULLY: it is Atlas's own field and 100 means NO discount (actual ===
origin). 70 means the row is currently discounted to 70% of list. It is a percentage OF the list
price, not off it.
WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS, so the next reader knows the diff is small: Atlas documenting a unit (a
`price.actual.unit` on every media row would do it), or a model page settling on one of its three
sentences. The transcription is already here; only the `unpriced` reason would come out and a
`unit` + `usd` pair go in.
Row shape:
unpriced  the REASON no rate can be stated, in prose. Present on every row today.
listed    { actual, origin, discount } — Atlas's own numbers, unit unknown.
source / verified
`bun run audit:atlascloud` re-reads the catalog weekly and reports when a listed figure moves.
